key_insight: MedCORE makes medical image diagnosis more interpretable by forcing the model to reason through clinician-style criteria, local evidence, and their relationships before predicting a label.
clinical_relevance: This could support safer, more transparent screening and grading by showing which morphological findings drive each diagnosis across different imaging modalities.
method: Decomposes diagnosis into explicit clinical criteria and localizes each criterion to relevant image regions.
Uses multi-scale visual encoders plus a Graph Attention Network to model dependencies between criteria.
Aligns visual criteria with clinical text, class prototypes, and uncertainty-weighted evidence aggregation.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on ISIC 2018, BUSI, and IDRiD, achieving strong reported performance including 89.2%/96.1%/84.3% accuracy and 96.4%/98.4%/92.8% AUC across the three datasets.
watch_item: The framework’s complexity and reliance on well-defined criteria, prototypes, and uncertainty calibration may make deployment and generalization harder in settings with limited annotations or shifting clinical protocols.
paper_title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis
